text: According to W. K. Clifford's 'ethics of belief,' it is epistemically and morally permissible to believe a proposition on insufficient evidence when the choice between hypotheses is forced, live, and momentous.
explanation: This is false: it describes William James's 'will to believe,' the reply to Clifford, not Clifford's own view. Clifford's thesis is the unconditional evidentialist prohibition: 'it is wrong always, everywhere, and for anyone, to believe anything upon insufficient evidence.' James introduces the forced-live-momentous conditions precisely to carve out an exception Clifford would reject.
